Train 1 leaves A at 09:10 toward B at 84 km/h. Distance A-B = 391 km. Train 2 leaves B at 10:05 toward A at 106 km/h. Bird starts at A together with first train and flies at 150 km/h back and forth between trains until they meet. Need when and where trains meet, and how far bird flies.

Need reason step by step and check every calculation.

Let's set time. Let t be hours after 09:10. Train1 position from A: x1 = 84 t, until meeting. Train2 leaves at 10:05, which is 55 min after 09:10 = 55/60 = 11/12 h. For t >= 11/12, train2 position from A: x2 = 391 - 106 (t - 11/12). Meeting when x1 = x2.

84 t = 391 - 106(t - 11/12) = 391 - 106t + 106*11/12. 106*11/12 = (106/12)*11 = 53/6*11 = 583/6 = 97.1666667. So RHS = 391 + 583/6 - 106t. 391 = 2346/6, sum = 2929/6. Equation: 84t = 2929/6 - 106t => 190t = 2929/6 => t = 2929/(1140) hours. Simplify? 2929/1140. 1140*2=2280 remainder649. 649/1140=0.569298. t=2.569298 h = 2h + 0.569298*60=34.1579 min = 2h34m9.47s. Meeting time 09:10 + 2:34:09.47 = 11:44:09.47. Check if after 10:05 yes.

Alternative compute after second train leaves: At 10:05, train1 has traveled 84*(55/60)=84*11/12=7*11=77 km. Distance remaining = 391-77=314 km. Relative speed = 84+106=190 km/h. Time after 10:05 = 314/190 = 157/95 h = 1.65263158 h = 1h39m9.47s. Add to 10:05 = 11:44:09.47. Same.

Meeting location from A: x1 = 84*t = 84*2929/1140 = simplify 84
